post.description: Computes a candidate calc rule now, on each owner it selects that the caller may read, with the reduce the tick runs, and writes nothing (a read-only transaction). For each owner it answers the value the rule would write, the output's current value and whether they differ, the inputs with no value, the members skipped and the instances left out as stale (named when the caller may read the component, else counted). An expression that reads one member's value by position (members[1].value.t, or an element of an input's list) over a system with a member the caller may not read is withheld on that system, its error counting the members out of scope; one that folds each input's list whole (avg(t), max(t)) shows the aggregate. A component rule previews the selected components holding one of its inputs, as the tick would mark them. The owners holding a current value of the output are computed first, so the cap never hides one, and the answer lists the owners holding a value or that the rule would write one on first, each by name. At most owner_cap owners are computed, and a bound on total input reads stops a preview over large systems early, a whole owner at a time (owners_judged of owners_total, truncated past either). The candidate is checked as a save would check it: a reduce that does not compile, a cycle in the key graph, an output another enabled rule or a collection writes, or health are each a 422, so the author learns before saving; given a saved rule's name it is judged as an edit of that rule. The selector's names resolve in the caller's read scope: a name that does not exist and one the caller may not read are the same 422, and a name shared in and out of scope means the one in scope. A preview takes no lock a save waits on. Gated by rule:read.

Bounded by the same two scopes the apply is, so it never lists a row the apply would then refuse to touch. A location preview also lists the components and systems placed at every location whose label would move, because those go stale the moment it does. Gated by location:update, the same permission the apply needs: a preview is half of an edit rather than a report, and an operator who cannot apply has no use for it.

Recorded as ONE audit row for the operation, naming the rule tier and the affected count, rather than one row per changed entity. Gated by location:update.

The uuid does not change, so every reference inside the platform still resolves and now reads the new name; a script or a bookmark that typed the old one stops resolving, which is why the rename is its own act and its own permission rather than a patch field. post.description: The webhook transport's listener (#1024): a component or a cloud service posts here, to the URL its webhook endpoint was given. The token names one endpoint; the scheme its driver declares authenticates the post (an hmac signature over a signed timestamp, a token, basic, or none, which reads unsigned); a signed timestamp outside five minutes is refused, and a declared delivery id lands once. The driver's listeners map the body (json, xml, form or text) onto any lane, and the post also lands as a log line unless its listener says otherwise. Public by necessity: the sender is not a principal, and the endpoint's scheme is the authentication. Answers 202 once the post is published, 401 for a refused scheme (saying nothing of which part failed), 404 for an unknown or rotated token (identical either way), 413 past 1 MiB, 429 with Retry-After past a rate limit.
